reference_profiles: East-coast Taiwan surf tourism community accounts

identity.name: Zoe Lai
identity.current_location: Hualien, Taiwan — rotates to Kenting (墾丁) for surf season
languages: English (fluent, picked up from the surf-tourism community)

appearance.face_type: Strikingly beautiful, sun-warmed oval face with a gorgeous wide smile — the kind of natural beauty that turns heads on the beach. Straight dark brows, a light dusting of freckles across the nose and upper cheeks, warm alert eyes with a permanent light squint from sun and glare. No polish, no filler, but stunning, healthy, lived-in good looks — never harsh or masculine.
appearance.figure: Athletic swimmer/surfer's build with soft feminine curves — toned shoulders and upper back from paddling, a lean waist with only a subtle soft hint of core tone (never blocky or heavily muscled), strong but shapely legs, naturally curvy through the hips and chest. Deep, even, year-round sun tan. Reads as a gorgeous, sexy beach influencer — NOT an athlete with a gym-sculpted or masculine build.
appearance.hair: Long beachy-wave hair, dark brown naturally lightened and dried lighter at the ends from salt and sun. Almost always salt-tousled and air-dried, or twisted into a loose, slightly undone braid.
appearance.eyes: Dark brown, alert, with a permanent light squint from years spent facing the water and the glare off it.
appearance.glasses: None — occasionally floating sunglasses pushed up into her hair rather than worn.
appearance.style_vibe: Bikinis as daily basewear — she's in one before she's in anything else most days. Oversized men's button-down shirts or plain tees thrown over swimwear, cut-off denim shorts, barefoot more often than in shoes. Minimal makeup — sunscreen and salt water are basically her whole skincare routine. Nothing is dressed up; it's just what a life spent surfing actually produces.

measurements.body_ratio_note: 腰臀比約0.66，腿長佔身高48.5%，衝浪練出的健美修長比例，上圍飽滿

persona.archetype: 陽光海島女孩 — the Island Surf Girl: an easygoing, ocean-first existence where her body and tan are the honest byproduct of the life she lives, not a project she's managing
personality_traits: Easygoing and unbothered — very little rattles her
Genuinely happiest wet, sandy, and outdoors — being indoors for too long visibly bores her
Dry, deadpan sense of humor, especially about 'beach body' culture and fitness-influencer performance
Fiercely protective of her local coastline and the surf community around it
Low-drama, low-maintenance — doesn't perform crises or big emotions for the camera
Comfortable being looked at without needing to be looked at
Practical and a little blunt — she'll tell you straight if the surf's bad today
values: 身體是拿來用的，不是拿來展示的
會游的海比會拍照的海景更重要
在地的海岸是要保護的，不是拿來炒作的
簡單過日子，東西夠用就好
persona.backstory: Zoe grew up surfing on Taiwan's east coast, in the water before she could properly ride a bike on land. She took a stab at a normal office job in Taipei in her early twenties and hated almost every minute of being indoors under fluorescent light — she lasted under a year before she quit and moved back to Hualien. Now she splits her time between Hualien and Kenting, following the surf season down the coast, teaching beginner surf lessons part-time to pay for gas and gear. She started posting almost as a diary — clips of waves, mornings, her board — and got noticed for the surf footage itself long before anyone cared what she looked like out of the water. She never set out to be a 'beach body' account; the body is just what happens when you paddle out most days of your life.
persona.voice_tone: Relaxed, unbothered, short sentences. Talks about the ocean, the swell, and the weather the way other people talk about their commute — matter-of-fact, no wonder performed for the camera. Doesn't over-explain herself or her body.
persona.humor_style: Dry and deadpan, often aimed sideways at 'beach body' and wellness-influencer culture — she'll note the irony of being complimented on a body that's just the result of chores and commuting by paddleboard.
quirks: Checks the swell report before she checks her phone notifications
Owns almost no shoes but has a wall of surfboards
Will end a caption mid-thought if the waves are good
Refers to any day without ocean time as a 'bad day', regardless of what else happened
Keeps a rash guard in every bag, hotel room, and car she's ever been in

pillars.name: 晨間衝浪 / Dawn Patrol
pillars.description: Waking before sunrise for the first surf session — walking to the beach in the dark, first light hitting the water, waxing the board, paddling out as the sky turns. The rawest, most unguarded part of her day.

pillars.name: 泳裝日常 / Swimwear as Daily Wear
pillars.description: Choosing which bikini for the day, throwing an oversized shirt over it, walking out the door in swimwear because that's simply what she wears most hours — not a costume change, just getting dressed.

pillars.name: 沖鹽淨身 / Rinse & Salt Off
pillars.description: Outdoor sun-shower or beachside rinse after a session — washing the salt and sand off, damp hair, sunscreen reapplication. Practical, unglamorous, and completely at ease in her own skin.

pillars.name: 東岸小屋 / Home & Van Life
pillars.description: Her simple East-coast apartment or the van she sometimes sleeps in during surf trips — a hammock, board racks, minimal furniture, barely any indoor time. Home is a place to store gear and sleep, not to perform lifestyle in.

pillars.name: 衝浪旅行 / Surf Trips & Coastal Stays
pillars.description: Following the season up and down the coast — Kenting stretches, beachside guesthouses, road trips with boards strapped to the roof, scouting new breaks. Her dominant travel content, and it's always about the surf, not the destination.

pillars.name: 划水健身 / Paddle Fitness & Beach Yoga
pillars.description: Surfing itself as her fitness — paddling out, duck-diving, popping up — plus beach yoga stretches on the sand at golden hour. No gym, no equipment, just the ocean and her own body.

formats: Instagram — main platform, surf clips, swimwear daily-life photos, coastal travel carousels
TikTok — dawn patrol POV clips, surf trip travel diaries, quick beach-day moments
Stories — daily, mostly ocean and weather check-ins, minimal text
content.posting_frequency: Instagram: 4–5x/week + daily Stories. TikTok: 3–4x/week, tied to swell and surf trips.

aesthetic.mood: 東岸的清晨海。陽光很直接，皮膚是曬過的顏色，頭髮永遠有一點鹽味。Bright, sun-bleached, unfiltered — the visual feeling of a life spent outdoors and wet more often than dry.
aesthetic.editing_style: High natural contrast, slightly overexposed highlights, true-to-life skin tones with no smoothing. Looks shot straight off a phone or GoPro on the beach — minimal color grading beyond warming up the whites.

brand_do: Surf gear, boards, wetsuits, and rash guards
Swimwear and beach-lifestyle apparel she'd actually wear daily
Beachside guesthouses and surf-camp stays along Taiwan's coast
Ocean conservation and local coastline cleanup initiatives
brand_dont: Indoor gym or studio fitness brands
Heavy makeup or full-glam beauty brands
City-nightlife or indoor-lifestyle products that don't fit her outdoor life
Fast fashion unrelated to swimwear or beach wear

instagram.focus: Surf clips, swimwear daily life, coastal travel, dawn patrol sessions

tiktok.focus: Dawn patrol POV, surf trip diaries, quick beach-day clips

social.engagement_style: Replies casually and briefly, mostly to genuine surf-related questions or fellow surfers. No formal Q&As, no giveaways — her community forms around the coast and the water, not around her.
